_why: Every on-disk shape a wish store has EVER written, replayed through the current reader on every commit. A version that loses data goes red BY NAME. See docs/WISH_STORES.md §6.
_provenance: SYNTHESISED from what the writers produce, not harvested from a played world. That is the weaker of the two and it is said out loud: a harvested corpus would also catch a shape the code can no longer produce but a child's disk still holds. Harvest into here from a real world as soon as one exists — `--harvest` on the test's tool.

⚠ FINDING, recorded not fixed. The ENVELOPE reads this fine — but ItemSpecStore.Spec.fromJson ends `fx.isEmpty() ? null : s`, so a design with no effects is written perfectly and rejected on the way back in. put() accepts one, so a store can hold a design that vanishes at the next world load. This case pins the envelope's half; the reader's half is docs/WISH_STORES.md §7. let a `plain`-shaped design with no effects back in (make_item mints those); this fixture's shape is `wand`, which the reader still drops.

The DESIGN only — no icon, no colour. Its look is item-icons-v1.json. item-specs-v1.json and items-v0-specs.json above are the shapes it migrates FROM, and ItemIconSplitTest replays both through the real store.

schemas._why: The newest schema each reader understands, so a store can move past v1 while its OLD fixtures keep replaying. A reader not named here is at v1. ItemIconSplitTest fails if this disagrees with the code's own constants.
